headline: Approved a car wash sign at 585 Pawtucket Boulevard and a 205-unit mixed-use development at 41 Hurd Street.
summary: The board also approved a variance for a home addition at 19 Lawton Street. Neighbors opposed the car wash sign, citing flood risk, chemicals, and traffic. Members said those issues belong to the Conservation Commission and Planning Board, and the sign approval requires no left turn signs at the driveways and two speed humps on Melrose Avenue.
decisions: Approved a variance for an addition at 19 Lawton Street, 5-0.
Approved a special permit and variance for an illuminated freestanding sign at 585 Pawtucket Boulevard, 5-0, with ten conditions.
Approved two variances for a 205-unit mixed-use development at 41 Hurd Street, 5-0, with four conditions.
Approved the minutes of the 10/15/2026 meeting, 5-0.

plain_text:
Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals Minutes 
10/26/2026 at 6:30 P.M.  
 
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, contact the Division of 
Development Services, 375 Merrimack Street, Lowell, MA or refer to video recordings available online 
at www.LTC.org. 
 
Members Present: Chairman Pech,  Member McCarthy, Member Procope, Member Briere, Member 
Hovey, Member Shanahan 
 
Members Absent:  
 
Others Present: Mary Brundage, Associate Planner 
 
The following represents the actions taken by the Zoning Board of Appeals at the 10/26/2026 meeting. 
This meeting was held in the  City Council Chambers. Attendees had the ability to participate via Zoom as 
permitted by Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, signed into law on March 28, 2025. 
 
Chairman Pech called the meeting to order at 6:30 PM. 
1. Continued Business 
 
  
2. New Business 
 
ZBA-2026-41  
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: Thyrin Song  
Property Located at: 19 Lawton Street, 01851  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals  will hold a public hearing to hear all interested 
persons relative to an application by Thyrin Song to construct an addition at 19 Lawton Street. The subject 
property is located in the Traditional  Two-Family (TTF) zoning district. The proposal requires a Variance 
per Section 5.1 for relief from minimum side yard setbacks and the minimum front yard setback and any 
other relief required under the City of Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Hushmann Afshar, Taj Engineering 
H. Afshar presented the project showing the proposed addition for a small storage area in the back of the 
existing house. The lot is on a corner lot and has two frontages, two side yard and no rear setbacks.  Right
now, there is a patio. The frontage is existing non-conforming for the house and addition. The existing 
side yard setback is 2.3 feet from the back corner of the building and 2.1 feet from the other corner of the 
building and proposed addition on the left side facing the home from Spring Street. The proposed addition 
will be set back four feet from Spring Street. The proposed addition will have its own shed roof. The 
applicant is proposing to extend it by 3’ 8” on one side and 6.5’ on the other side. The rest will be a new 
patio. The siding will match the existing house. The distance between the addition and the house behind 
it is 30 feet. The proposal is not of huge consequence to the area or detrimental to the neighborhood. 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
In Support: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
T. Hovey stated that he  does not see it as a major ask, not extending beyond the existing footprint. He 
does not think there is a significant change to what’s on site. 
 
M. Briere did not have any questions. 
 
G. Procope agreed that it does not look like it will be any impediment toward the neighborhood. He asked 
what the storage would be used for. H. Afshar responded that it would be for bicycles and household 
items. G. Procope asked about the legal notice on the front of the door.  H. Afshar explained that a 
handyman started the work and the building department issued a legal notice. H. Afshar explained to the 
applicant that he would have to come before the Board. G. Procope asked if the issue will be resolved 
after they receive approval.  H. Afshar responded that it would. 
 
D. McCarthy noted that the construction looks like it is almost complete. H. Afshar confirmed that it was 
close to complete. He mentioned that there are two different dimensions between the site plan and the 
floor plan. H. Afshar confirmed that the site plan has the correct dimensions. D. McCarthy mentioned that 
it is on quiet, dead street and does not have a significant impact.  He noted that is not typical to ask for a 
variance after building. 
 
D. Shanahan stated that the same setback will be maintained and did not have any issue with the request. 
 
V. Pech agreed that that the request is minimal. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to issue the Variance. Seconded by T. Hovey. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-42  
Petition Type: Variance and Special Permit  
Applicant: Aim Realty Medford, LLC  
Property Located at: 585 Pawtucket Boulevard, 01854  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 6.3.2(9) and Section 6.3.2(8)  
Petition:  Aim Realty Medford, LLC has applied to Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals for Special Permit 
approval for internal illumination and to install a free -standing sign. The subject property is in the 
Suburban Mixed Use (SMU) zoning district. The application requires Special Permit approval under Section
6.3.2 (9) for internal illumination and Variance approval under Section 6.3.2(8) to install a free -standing 
sign with each face area exceeding thirty (30) square feet, and for any other relief required under the 
Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
John Cox, Attorney 
Matt Hamor, Landplex 
 
J. Cox explained there is currently a purchase and sale agreement with the owners of the property at 585 
Pawtucket Boulevard, the AAA building. There is approximately 30,000 square feet of land. The company, 
Scrub-a-Dub operates state-of-the-art car washes throughout New England. It’s a family-owned business 
for over 60 years. For the project to move forward, approvals are needed from the Zoning Board of 
Appeals, the Planning Board and Conservation Commission. Looking for a Special Permit approval to install 
two illuminated signs, one is on the building, and one is freestanding. The freestanding sign face exceeds 
30 square feet; the sign face would be 41.25 square feet. The sign will only be 16 feet high, lower what 
the district would allow at 20 feet. The relief requested is strictly for the freestanding sign and illumination. 
The car wash would close at 8 PM every night, Sunday at 6PM. It’s 24-hour surveillance and 24/7 security 
with locked gates. He stated that they met with the Pawtucketville neighborhood association and one of 
the concerns was on Melrose Street with cars coming out of the car wash . They had agreed to put a no 
left turn sign on the exit and would work with city on potentially adding sp eed bumps. Currently there is 
no car wash in Pawtucketville and this would be a great asset to neighb orhood and city. The investment 
would be upwards of $8 million so the tax revenue would be substantial. They have met with  the traffic 
engineer and had a traffic study done. The traffic engineer’s comments are on the comment memo dated 
October 21. It states that the applicant has committed to the following on-site and off-site mitigation, no 
left-hand turn and construction of speed bumps. The trip generation plan seems to be satisfied. There are 
nine proposed conditions on the memo, mostly for the Planning Board. The applicant is agreeable to those 
conditions.  
 
In Opposition: 
John Hamblet, 495 Varnum Avenue 
J. Hamblet requested the board to deny the variance request. The objection comes from concerns with 
public safety. The sign will be in a regulatory floodway. This part of the city has been hit with two 100 -
year floods in the last 20 years. After the devasting Mother’s Day flood in 2006, the City created the flood 
plain overlay district to make sure past mistakes are not repeated. The stormwater report shows that the 
project is in the zone AE which is a special flood hazard zone. Under Section 9.1.3 it is clear that the rules 
of this overlay district override everything else. Section 9.1.7 paragraph 2 states that in Zone AE along 
water course that have a regulatory floodway , and the Merrim ack River is a federally designated as a 
floodway, all encroachments are prohibited including in the flood plain. A sign requires a structural 
foundation, which means putting fill in a protected floodway. Because the zoning laws completely ban 
this to prevent dangerous water displacement, there is no legal path to grant a variance. 
 
Francis Espinola, 60 Melrose Avenue 
F. Espinola states s everal years ago  he was denied extending the back deck by two feet because of the 
conservation area. The plot of land behind the  property on Shirley Avenue, they’ve been trying to build 
there for over 20 years. No one has been able to due to conservation. 
 
Local residents can’t expand or people can’t build residential  in the neighborhood. Are we supposed to 
approve signage which leads to everything else for a building in good standing to tear it down and  build
something larger? They need to build a large wall to block headlights. Main concern is if the neighborhood 
can’t even put in a shed but should be allowing this? 
 
Michael Ward 36 Melrose Avenue 
M. Ward stated that he was worried about groundwater being displaced into his yard and we don’t need 
a car wash in the neighborhood. 
 
Carlton Jones, 53 Melrose Avenue 
C. Jones stated that a c ar wash in a residential area not a good idea. He expressed c oncern about the 
contaminants from the property. His property is 150 feet from where the planned car wash is. Putting in 
speed bumps are not going to solve the problem. People are not going to pay attention to a no left turn 
sign. He stated that he opposes this project very strongly. 
 
Pat Reilly, 60 Melrose Avenue 
P. Reilly stated that t raffic on street is horrible there. She expressed concern with kids on bikes in the 
neighborhood, a car wash in residential area shouldn’t be there. It’s in a flood plain , we can’t cut a tree 
down without getting proper permission which isn’t granted. 
 
Jake Higgins, 59 Melrose Avenue 
J. Higgins stated that he is also opposed to the car wash. Earlier this year, he attempted to get permits to 
build a shed on his property and was denied.  He expressed concern about chemicals from the 
establishment in the event of a flood and coming through the neighborhood. Lots of people have gardens.  
 
Ray Pelletier, 77 Lexington Avenue 
R. Pelletier stated that he has lived there for 60 years and remembers that area being nice and quiet. Lot 
of traffic has come through in the past 5 to 10 years and accidents in front of his house. It doesn’t make 
sense to have extra vehicles coming through there.  
 
In Support: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
V. Pech asked the applicant to  address some of the comments regarding  the potential chemicals and 
traffic and flood zone. M. Hamor responded that they are in the flood plain and that the project that 
consisted of three units, yet to be built, was fully permitted. That is an example of a proper ty that was 
able to meet the standards of the MA DEP in order to work in the floodplain. That process will be played 
out for this project at the Conservation C ommission meeting scheduled for November where they will 
meet those performance standards necessary for this project to be permitted. There is no net effect to 
this development from what’s there today. The volume that’s displaced on that property is going to be no 
more with this proposed development. In terms of traffic, there is a memo prepared by a traffic engineer. 
They have met with the city traffic engineers, and it was determined that there was going to be no net 
negative impact to the surrounding roadways and mitigation was discussed at the meeting. It will be 
further discussed at the Planning Board meeting. 
 
M. Hamor explained that the sign will be lower than what is allowed in that district. The use is allowed in 
the district through an issuance of a permit through the Planning Board. The  volume of water being 
displaced in terms of whether you can put the sign there will be covered through the Conservation 
Commission proceedings.
J. Cox pointed that the district is a mixed suburban use and that there are businesses along Pawtucket 
Boulevard, bigger than what is proposed. He also mentioned that they are not proposing tearing down 
the existing building. He reiterated that the request is for the construction of a freestanding sign and the 
illumination of two signs, the conservation issues will be handle d at the commission meeting. He 
mentioned that they also presented at the neighborhood association meeting. 
 
M. Briere stated that he hears the concerns of neighbors however those concerns are not being asked to 
be addressed by this board . Other regulatory boards, namely the Conservation Commission and will 
render the ultimate authority for the business to exist. What is being asked of the board is concerning an 
illuminated sign which he is supportive of. 
 
G. Procope agreed that they can only  vote on what is in front of us. In his opini on, he felt asking for the 
sign before the going through the other boards would be putting the cart before the horse. If anything, 
he’d be in favor of a continuance. 
 
D. McCarthy echoed the same concerns with approving the sign before the Planning Board approval. That 
said, the existing AAA looks the same size as what is being proposed. M. Hamor pointed out that the round 
portion on the top of the sign is what throws it over the allowable limit.  A lot of time and effort was put 
into the design of the entire sign, and it is the same one used at the other facilities.  
  
D. Shananan agreed that their job is limited in scope to what is before them which is the requested 
variance for the signage. He did agree that the no left turn sign was only as good as the people who would 
obey it, but it is out of the scope here. A s far as the signage, this is a great sign for car washes. The black 
with the illuminated letters would be very subtle. He asked about the hours of operation. J. Cox responded 
that hours would be 7:30 to 8 Monday – Saturday, 8 to 6, Sunday. The sign would shut off at 10PM. 
 
T. Hovey stated that he appreciated the neighbors’ concerns but those should be brought up at the other 
land use boards. There is not an issue with the proposed sign and there is no reason to deny this. 
 
V. Pech stated that he appreciated abutters coming to the meeting. He stated they were here specifically 
for the illumination and signage. He agreed with his colleagues that usually the approvals will go through 
the other land use boards but we’re just voting on the sign and the illumination. He asked if the applicant 
was amenable to the proposed conditions. J. Cox confirmed. 
 
D. McCarthy added that a condition that the hours of illumination be one hour before sunrise to no later 
than 10PM. 
 
Motion: 
G. Procope motioned to approve the Special Permit for internal illumination and the Variance to install a 
free-standing sign with each face area exceeding thirty (30) square feet with the following conditions: 
 
1. The existing  building's water, sewer, and gas services will need to be cut and capped at their 
respective mains as part of the demolition. The applicant shall indicate the locations of the 
existing services on the site plan and add a note indicating that they will be cut and capped at the 
mains;
2. All utility trenches within the City right-of-way will need to be milled and paved in one continuous 
patch. The applicant shall indicate the limits of the proposed mill-and-pave restoration on the site 
plan; 
3. The applicant shall obtain all applicable permits from the City Engineer's Office for water, sewer, 
drainage, trench, street opening, and driveway work. All work requiring Engineering Department 
inspections must be inspected by the City; 
4. The existing paved parking area along Melrose Avenue will need to be removed and replaced with 
grass or landscaping. The applicant shall show the proposed restoration on the site plan; 
5. The applicant shall install an additional  oil & grease separator should be installed in place of 
proposed drain manhole with inv. 94.9; 
6. The applicant shall obtain a stormwater permit prior to construction; 
7. The Applicant shall commit to the following off-site mitigation: 
a) No Left Turn signage at the site driveways to prevent left turns onto Melrose Avenue; and 
b) Construction of two (2) speed humps on Melrose Avenue to be placed between the site 
driveways and Malden Avenue to be effective in reducing speeds; 
8. The applicant shall use the existing WYE on Melrose Avenue for the sewer service connection; 
9. The applicant shall provide flow calculations; and 
10. The hours of illumination for the signs shall be one hour before sunrise and no later than 10PM. 
Seconded by T. Hovey . The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-43  
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: New England Heritage Properties, Inc  
Property Located at: 41 Hurd Street, 01852  
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 9.8.6(1) and Section 9.8.6(7)  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by New England Heritage Properties, Inc to construct a 205 -unit mixed -use 
development at 41 Hurd Street. The subject property is located in the Downtown Mixed-Use (DMU) zoning 
district and Multi -Family Overlay – Mid Rise (MFOM) Overlay District. The project requires Variance 
approval per Section 9.8.6(1) for relief from the ground floor uses and entrance requirements, per Section 
9.8.6(7) for  relief from the motor vehicle access and parking requirements, and for any other relief 
required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
John Geary, Attorney 
 
J. Geary explained that the applicant was the successful responded to the City’s RFP to redevelop 41 Hurd 
Street, the site of the former District Court. They are seeking two variances , one which requires each 
ground floor unit within the midrise multifamily overlay district have direct access to the outside street 
level and one that generally prohibits surface parking between the street and building. The property is at 
the intersections of Hurd, George and Williams Streets. The property contains  about 57,000 square feet 
of land. It’s located in the Downtown Mixed-Use district (DMU) and the Multi-Family Overlay – Mid Rise 
(MFOM) district. They have presented to the historic board and received a major development permit to 
demolish the existing court house structure and construct a six -story mixed use development consisting 
of 205 residential units, two commercial units, sur face parking, on -site amenities and landscaping. The 
applicant anticipates investing about $76 million t o redevelop as proposed.  The requested relief only
concerns the ground floor design of four residential units and the surface parking. Otherwise, the proposal 
is zoning compliant. The project will require site plan review approval from the Planning Board. 
 
J. Geary stated effective July 1, 2026, Mass General Laws, Chapter 48 Section 10 requires the Zoning Board 
of Appeals must grant the variance if it find s the strict enforcement of the ordinance would result in a 
practical difficulty to the applicant. In making that the determination, the Board must weigh the benefits 
to the applicant and to the public interest including the production of housing against the detriment of 
the public health, safety, and welfare of the neighborhood the property is part of. The Board may also 
consider w hether the practical difficulty relates to soil conditions, shape and topography of the lot, 
whether strict enforcement would impose a financial hardship on the applicant, whether the benefit can 
be achieved by some other means or whether the practical difficulty was self-created. 
 
J. Geary explained that Sec. 9.8.6 (1) requires that the ground floor units have direct access to the street 
level. The requested relief is for all 10 first floor ground level units. Eight of those units will open to exterior 
by way of a small patio. Two of the units will not have any access to the street at all. Those two units are 
along George Street. In this instance, strict enforcement of the  ordinance would create a practical 
difficulty for the applicant. The parcel has three frontages and changes grades . Requiring ten separate 
exterior entrances onto street level would complicate the relationship between the units and the sloping 
sidewalks and would result ing in an inefficient redesign of the development and potentially affect the 
redevelopment of this property. The benefits to the applicant and the public are substantial, creating 205 
new residential units, two commercial spaces and reusing a vacant courthouse site.  The applicant is 
improving the streetscape and adding residents to the downtown. Eight of ten residential units on the 
ground floor do have access to an exterior patio, only two do not. All of the residential ground units have 
safe interior access through the common area. 
 
J. Geary explained that the second relief requested for Section 9.8.6 (7) generally prohibits surface parking 
between the building frontage and the street. The prop osed parking provides a courtyard like parking 
service area between Hurd Street and the building. Strict enforcement of this section would also create a 
practical difficulty for the same re asons mentioned. The geometry of this lot with the three frontages , 
grade changes  and limited access points require the building garage entrance, pedestrian routes, 
landscaping and parking within a constrained footprint in the downtown area makes it difficult. Removing 
or relocating the surface parking spaces would require a material redesign of the project and jeopardize 
any feasibility of a reasonable amount of off-street parking for this mixed-use development. The required 
balancing also fa vors this relief. The project’s public and private benefits including substantial housing 
production, commercial activity production, productive reuse of a  long vacant downtown lot and 
additional tax revenue to the City.  The surface parking area will be screened by a red brick wall and will 
have landscaping surrounding it. There’s no detriment looking down the street from the streetsca pe of 
the property. 
 
J. Geary stated that the s taff comments are supportive of this proposal. The  MFOM district does not 
require parking. The proposal will be providing 36 parking spaces and is close proximity to a couple of 
municipal parking garages. There are a few engineering conditions, those comments w ill be addressed 
with the Planning Board. DPD staff believes the project will enhance the area , provide much needed 
housing to the City, and will be an economic boost to the neighborhood. 
 
Jeffrey Bush, New England Heritage Properties 
J. Bush presented the architectural plans to the board. The mandates of the RFP were to create density of 
housing and commercial activation along the first floor if possible. He explained there will be 10 residential
units and two commercial spaces on the first floor along with visitor and guest parking along the front of 
the building on Hurd Street. Due to the unique characteristics of the site, the development is oriented on 
Hurd Street which is the main thoroughfare in the neighborhood. In doing so, they stepped the building 
off the back of the sidewalk in the middle portion of the  building. This creates a strong urban edge that 
recognizes the historic significance of that street and the importance of a pedestrian friendly viewpoint. 
It also creates some visual buffer from traffic and a safe ingress /egress for the parking in front of the 
building. There is also some parking along the back of the building within a contained garage. It is limited 
in scope relative to the project primarily because the City has a parking garage directly across from Hurd 
Street. They are in negotiations with the City for an access agreement for parking spaces for the residents 
in that garage. Some parking is provided to alleviate the coming and going of tenants as well as commercial 
tenants and visitors. 
 
Brian Geaudreau, Hancock Engineering 
B. Geaudreau explained that the site is bound by three streets: Hurd Street to the north, George Street to 
the east and Williams Street to the south. This led to the variance request for the parking in front of the 
facade. There’s really no practical way  to provide parking outside of the garage space. The wall on Hurd 
Street provides a buffer. Topographically Williams Street is higher than Hurd and George Streets. There is 
about 6 feet of elevation change. The elevation change is why there is a variance request for the ten units 
on the ground floor. There is no practical way to get those units down to the street level. Currently there 
is no stormwater management system on site. With courthouse coming down, they have an oppo rtunity 
to redevelop the site and bring it into compliance with current standards. There will be infiltration system 
underneath the parking lot. They are current ly working with both city engineering and Lowell regional 
wastewater for the stormwater permit. All the utilities that su pport the site are on the surrounding 
streets. There is also exterior amenity space for residents that will not be paved. 
 
J. Geary pointed out that the strict adherence for the specific zoning codes would present a practical 
difficulty for applicant and therefore they are requesting the two variances.  
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
In Support: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
 
G. Procope stated that he can support this project and that the area needs to be redeveloped. He felt that 
request was warranted. It will add some needed light to that area. He does not see a problem with 
approving both variances as long as the applicant is willing to meet the conditions. 
 
D. McCarthy stated that project is amazing. He asked why they decided to incorporate the parking. J. Bush 
responded that it was mostly for convenience factor for some residents who want parking within the 
building and so providing covered parking in that area does not lend itself to another obvious use. They 
will be asking for a vote from  City Council for a loading zone in front of that building. D. McCarthy asked 
about the dumpster in the front yard. J. Bush responded that there are two dumpsters provided on the 
first floor in front of the building which are related to the commercial uses. The provision is allowed for a 
truck to be able to pick it up and remove it. They would be shielded by an extension of the landscaping 
wall. The main resident ial dumpsters are in the back of the building within a trash room, so it won’t be
stored outside openly. D. McCarthy asked what the amenity inside the building they are proposing. J. Bush 
responded that it will probably some small fitness amenities, some location for work from home and some 
community area for residents , along with some outdoor living space. D. McCarthy asked if the units are 
going to primarily one-bedroom. J. Bush responded that it will be a majority of one-bedroom mixed with 
studios and two-bedrooms. There is a lot of demand for young professionals and couples as well as empty 
nesters that tend to be served by apartment complexes. Those mixes would meet the need well.  D. 
McCarthy stated that he is very supportive of the two variances with the proposed conditions. 
 
D. Shanahan agreed that it was a good -looking building and that the development fits into the character 
of the neighborhood. With regard to the exterior entrances, he feels that it is safer for the residents if 
they have a controlled ingress/egress through the interior of the building. He is in favor of the request. 
 
T. Hovey mentioned that the City parking garage generally has two empty floors. He asked if the parking 
in front would be reserved for commercial visitors and employees and visitors to the facility. J. Bush 
responded that it will probably be labeled. It will not meet the need for the entirety of the commercial 
spaces so it will not be exclusively for that but doesn’t foresee it for overnight residential parking. T. Hovey 
doesn’t have any concerns  and that project will bring some life to that corridor. He stated that he is in 
support of this project. 
 
M. Briere thanked New England Heritage Properties for investing in the City. He stated that the plans are 
spectacular and looks forward to seeing the enhancement that this will bring to the downtown landscape. 
He stated that he is in favor. 
 
V. Pech agreed that this is a  great investment for the City and that’s a big addition to the neighborhood 
and downtown. He is happy to support this as well. He asked of the applicant was amenable to the 
conditions laid out in the memo. J. Geary confirmed they were. 
 
Motion 
G. Procope motioned to approve the Variances with the following conditions: 
1. The applicant shall provide a detailed utility plan subject to Engineering Department approval; 
2. The applicant shall cut and cap the water and sewer services at the mains prior to demolition; 
3. The applicant shall replace existing sidewalks along the perimeter of the property with new 
concrete; and 
4. The applicant shall obtain a Stormwater Permit from the LRWWU. 
M. Briere seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
3. Other Business 
Minutes for Approval:   
10/15/2026 
 
G. Procope motioned to approve the minutes. Seconded by D. McCarthy. 
 
The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
Adjournment
G. Procope motioned to adjourn. Seconded by D. McCarthy. Adjourned at 7:51 PM.
